Codex is one of the most important untold stories in the history of technology.

A year ago, OpenAI’s coding effort looked lost in the wilderness:

 * Codex Cloud had flopped.
 * Their $3 billion Windsurf deal fell apart.
 * Claude Code was running away with the market.

Less than 12 months later, a tiny team in the “backwaters” of OpenAI built an app that grew to more than 40 million users, swallowed ChatGPT from the inside, and remade the entire company.

I had a front-row seat to the whole arc—from a conference room in their office the night before GPT-5 launched to the day Codex took over ChatGPT—and spent months interviewing the people who made it happen, including OpenAI’s Greg Brockman and Thibault “Tibo” Sottiaux. It’s a wild story about what it takes to build when the frontier is moving beneath your feet:
